page.layout: One block of running text with a heading line above it, followed by a three-column table (Indica, Chaldaica, Latina) and a closing paragraph below. The running head is at the top centre. No margin notes. A catchword stands at the right below the last line.

main_text.p: est Miserere super me, Domine: quoniam eo-ram te orabo tota die: laetifica animam servi tui. In hoc versu duas tantùm voces reperi-es Indianae linguae cum Chaldaicis congruentes, nempe chulo & lanasscha[?]. Sed ut clarius harum linguarum affinitas tibi pateat & diversitas, apponam ex utraque vocabula quaedam cum rerum interpretatione:

Hinc facile est judicare linguam, quam Indianam vocant, non esse Chaldaicam: nisi contra claram scripturam sentire velis, Danielem, Onkelon, Ionathan, & reliquos orientales interpretes, non Chaldaicè, sed fortasse Callicuticè scripsisse.

page.notes: The first word of the page, "est", is a fragment carried over from the previous page. Doubtful readings are marked [?]: "lanasscha" (italic, the ligature-like letters are hard to separate), "Gabiâ", "Ehâjta", and "Tebârâ" (the Chaldaic cells are small and partly smudged). The accents on the Chaldaic words are as far as I could make them out. The "Fregisti." cell is partly cut by the fold and the right edge. The final catchword "Est" is at the right edge; its letters are partly cut off. No page number is printed.
